response.title: which enclosed 3d printer has the fewest failed prints
response.answer:
If your top priority is the fewest failed prints, I would focus on Bambu Lab's enclosed CoreXY printers, particularly the P1S, X1 Carbon, and newer H2 series.

Bambu Lab has a strong reputation for reliable, low-maintenance printing thanks to automatic bed leveling, calibrated print profiles, and integrated hardware and software.

However, there's an important distinction: No manufacturer publishes independently verified, comparable print-failure rates across all enclosed 3D printers. So it's not possible to prove which printer has the absolute lowest failure rate.

The best choice also depends on whether you're printing PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA, or engineering materials.

My top choices
Shop

1. Bambu Lab P1S

Best proven value

Excellent reliability for PLA, PETG, ABS and ASA. A hands-on reviewer reported approximately 5% failures over 1,617 printing hours. 
Additive Realm

$449.99

Shop

2. Bambu Lab H2D

Premium option with a heated chamber, dual nozzles and advanced automation. Promising for demanding materials, but insufficient comparative data to establish a lower failure rate.

$1,399.00

Shop

3. Prusa CORE One+

Strong alternative if you value long-term repairability, support and consistent operation. Its actual failure-rate advantage over Bambu is unproven.

$1,149.00

One interesting dataset covering more than 560,000 user-reported print outcomes ranked the Bambu P1 and X1 families favorably, but its reporting biases mean the figures aren't controlled failure-rate measurements.
